calls.title: Contextual Bandit Check in
calls.summary: The team discussed significant updates to the contextual bandits system, prioritizing a robust refactor of variation weight pairing led by Teresa Yung, which enhances SDK safety. They completed the decoupling of experiment logic, simplifying the frontend. Notably, returning users will benefit from seed re-randomization to dynamically adjust to better performing arms. Integration of Statistical Reliability Monitoring (SRM) was also covered, with debates on including variation weights in event queries. The team agreed to require a bandit period ID for context-specific event analysis. They also favored separating contextual bandit exposure queries into a new data model for clearer validation. Insights on algorithm improvements were shared, including a shift to Gauss Hermite quadrature and the development of shell scripts for bandit testing enhancements.
calls.keywords: contextual bandits, variation weights, SRM, exposure assignment query, bandit period ID, integration method

calls.title: Contextual Bandit Check in
calls.summary: The meeting focused on streamlining the contextual bandit data model by removing phases to treat data as the current state, aligning with team feedback. A plan to consolidate weight queries into a single query was proposed to reduce overhead and improve performance. Emphasis was placed on handling variation IDs to ensure consistent weight mapping even during changes. Additionally, discussions highlighted the need for clarity in SDK payload structures while maintaining performance efficiency. Efforts to eliminate legacy experiment-related code were also underway, led by Teresa, to simplify the codebase. The team expressed a desire to deepen their understanding of the Thompson sampling algorithm, prioritizing data model stability as they progress.

calls.title: Contextual Bandit Check in
calls.summary: The team met to design a new, dedicated data model for contextual bandits, emphasizing the necessity of a separate rule type to avoid confusion with legacy systems. Key discussions included the need for stable, deterministic context IDs derived from attribute rules for accurate tracking, as well as implementing historical tracking of bandit weight updates for trend analysis. Strategies to handle leaf-level errors through aggregation were proposed to ensure system robustness. The architecture plan involved separate snapshot and event collections for efficient data management. Additionally, customer-specified update schedules were outlined, allowing for flexibility, with further emphasis on early development of API endpoints for manual updates prior to UI work.
calls.keywords: Contextual Bandit, Data Model, Snapshot, Rule Type, SDK Payload, Agenda Job
